Tests whether the global step is a false positive. 1.51 dB below the same blur with contrast1 (pair0) -> global step is justified.
residual_intensity_corr=0.459 + gamma_suspect=True suggested a tone-curve (gamma) step; unique_G became 249 vs target 246 (1%.) but mean brightening overshoots (PSNR 22.66, lowest) -> rejected.

analysis.mode: PSNR for deterministic re-simulations (no noise step in candidate), SIGNAL history retained; raw sigma 3.95 (pair0) is JPEG-artifact inflated, cross-pair sigma 1.1/0.4 and peeled residual (spatial_corr=0.977, var_slope=-0.074) -> NO_NOISE
analysis.decision_rule: Deterministic candidates need PSNR > 40 dB or +2 dB vs previous round. Best new candidate (gaussian chain) is -0.45 dB vs R0 on all 3 pairs; R0 chain itself 25.55 dB mean -> NO_CHANGE.
signal_reinterpretation: blur_glass is stochastic: x_distortion/blur.py calls shuffle_pixels_njit with np.random.randint per pixel. Therefore (a) PSNR/self-simulation of any glass pipeline saturates ~25 dB, (b) the 11-21% block_boundary deficit of glass5+jpeg4 vs target is partly irreducible shuffle-realisation variance, and (c) the 3/3-pair raw spectral_slope match of glass (-1.417/-1.60/-1.70 vs target -1.379/-1.594/-1.678, diff 0.03-0.06) remains the strongest subtype evidence. PSNR ordering glass > gaussian on 3/3 pairs (+0.58/+0.52/+0.26 dB) confirms the R0 choice.

Global step: variance_ratio=0.456 / spread 0.6385 / chroma 0.7855 / mean_shift=+5.4. Relative to blur+JPEG baseline the missing tone step is var x0.72-0.75, i.e. c~0.85, milder than the mildest library contrast (sev1 c=0.75). No library function matches exactly: contrast1 after JPEG gives var 0.358 (closest variance; PSNR +1.51 dB over no-global), gamma sev1 matches unique_G (249 vs 246) but overshoots mean and costs 2.2 dB, saturate_weaken_HSV/D sev1 over-desaturate (chroma 0.605 vs 0.786), quantization_hist/median would collapse unique_G to <=24 (target 246) -> ruled out. Keep contrast_weaken_scale:1.
Order: contrast AFTER JPEG confirmed again - before JPEG raised bb +40% in R0 T9; after JPEG leaves bb unchanged and gives the best PSNR on all tested chains.

Noise re-check (R1 full_analysis reproduced: sigma 3.95, ric 0.4586, gamma_suspect=True): the intensity-correlated residual is explained by the tone step (gamma_suspect is a by-product), not by noise; cross-pair sigma 1.1/0.4 makes a sensor-noise step impossible.
analysis.severity_scan: blur: gaussian5, glass5, lens5 (R0), glass5 PSNR-checked on k=3; jpeg 4 (5 overshoots bb +58%); global: contrast1 (closest), gamma1, sat HSV1/3 (R0), no-global
analysis.residual_uncertainty: Library gap: GT global step (effective c~0.85, mean +5.4) cannot be represented exactly; contrast sev1 overshoots variance/unique_G while mean stays +2.0 vs +5.4. Glass-vs-gaussian remains a cross-signal conflict (slope/gm/gm-glass_score -> glass; bb magnitude -> gaussian), arbitrated by k=3 PSNR in favour of glass by only 0.45 dB. Training PSNR (R0=20.15) likely reflects this representability gap rather than a wrong degradation family.
